title: A Bug Erased $440 Million in 45 Minutes #shorts
description:
On August 1, 2012, Knight Capital pushed new trading software to its servers. One server was missed. Forty-five minutes later, the firm had lost four hundred and forty million dollars.
Follow for more true stories of fortunes made and lost.
first_comment: Who's to blame: the engineer who missed one server, or the firm that had no kill switch? 👇

lines.text: On August first, twenty twelve, a Wall Street firm lost four hundred and forty million dollars in forty-five minutes.
Not to a crash. Not to fraud. To a software update.
The firm was Knight Capital, one of the biggest traders in America.
That morning, engineers installed new code on eight servers.
The eighth still held a dead program from two thousand and three.
At nine thirty, the market opened, and the old code woke up.
It started buying and selling stocks like crazy. Millions of orders, and nobody could stop it.
There was no kill switch. Traders watched it burn money in real time.
In forty-five minutes, it lost four hundred and forty million dollars. More than the firm was worth.
Knight survived only with a four hundred million dollar rescue, and was sold a year later.
One missed server. One company gone.
Follow for more true stories of fortunes made and lost.
